about: The plan of the screenshot tour for the owner's review. The tour scene writes build/tour/<id>.png at 1920 x 1080 for every shot it can make, in this order, from the default town (seed 1), and build/tour/shots.json: this same structure with 'made': true or false per shot, 'shows' corrected to what is really on screen, and a 'wrong' note where the picture shows a fault. The questions are the lead's and stay as they are unless a shot shows something different from what the question asks about.

shots.shows: The start: one cottage, the well, one faint trail and one villager.
shots.question: Is this the right way to start?

shots.shows: The first delivery: the coin number rises where the water is delivered.
shots.question: Is the moment of earning clear enough?

shots.shows: The whole interface at level 1: coin and level bar, the next gift and the hint on the left, the shop on the right, the bell, achievements and pause at the bottom.
shots.question: Is the interface the right size and in the right places?

shots.shows: A second villager has been bought and walks the trail.
shots.question: Does buying a villager show clearly on the map?

shots.shows: After Pace and the Basket: villagers walk faster and carry a visibly bigger load.
shots.question: Can you see what these two upgrades did?

shots.shows: The shop close up: a line you can buy, one that needs more coin with its bar, one locked until a later level, one finished, each with what it is worth in coin a minute.
shots.question: Does each shop line tell you enough to choose?

shots.shows: Extend mode: the cottages that can be extended light up and the pointed one shows its price.
shots.question: Is extending a cottage by clicking it clear?

shots.shows: The same cottage after two extensions, beside a plain one.
shots.question: Can you tell an extended cottage from a plain one?

shots.shows: A building offer bought: the market stall stands on its staked plot.
shots.question: Is it clear that the stall was your purchase and where it went?

shots.shows: The bell is ringing: everyone hurries and the bell shows its rest time.
shots.question: Is the bell worth having as something to do with your hands?

shots.shows: People keep queueing at a workplace, so the shop offers an extra hand there and a marker shows where.
shots.question: Is it clear why this offer appeared?

shots.shows: A level is reached: the banner names the gift and the new cottage and lane appear.
shots.question: Is a new level enough of a moment?

shots.shows: Staked plots with labels show what comes next and at which level.
shots.question: Do the staked plots look right (not like an editor's boxes)?

shots.shows: The first field has arrived and villagers carry Grain.
shots.question: Does the town now read as doing two kinds of work?

shots.shows: A choice of two: the town keeps only the boon you pick.
shots.question: Is this kind of choice what you want more of?

shots.shows: A request is running: who asks, how much of what, how much is delivered, the time left and the reward.
shots.question: Do requests give you something to aim for?

shots.shows: A small touch has appeared by itself beside a cottage (a woodpile, a washing line or the like).
shots.question: Do these small touches make the town feel alive?

shots.shows: The mill works: its sails turn and villagers carry Flour to the market.
shots.question: Does the mill look and read right?

sections.title: A road wearing in, then paved

shots.shows: A road just given: a faint trail.
shots.question: Is a new road faint enough to look unworn but clear enough to see?

shots.shows: The same road after villagers have used it: a firm earth track.
shots.question: Can you see that it has worn in?

shots.shows: Pave mode: the roads that can be paved light up, the pointed one shows its price, the busiest is tagged.
shots.question: Is paving by clicking a road clear?

shots.shows: The same road paved with gravel.
shots.question: Does gravel look right?

shots.shows: A road in cobbles beside a gravel one and an earth track.
shots.question: Can you tell the three surfaces apart at a glance?

shots.shows: A crowded unpaved road: people bunch up and the road is tinted.
shots.question: Is it clear that this road is crowded and that paving would help?

sections.title: The end of the first age

shots.shows: The charter drive: the last great request of the age, filling in parts.
shots.question: Is this a good last push instead of a wait?

shots.shows: The whole town at the end of the first age.
shots.question: Does the finished hamlet look like a place you built?

shots.shows: The charter is granted: the stone stands on the green.
shots.question: Is the charter enough of a moment?

shots.shows: The achievements page, opened with Tab.
shots.question: Are the achievements the right kind of goals?

sections.title: The age change and the river

shots.shows: Ringing in the next age: the page turns to the town on the river.
shots.question: Is the age change enough of a moment?

shots.shows: The page that opens the second age and says what is new.
shots.question: Does this page tell you what you need?

shots.shows: High water: a boat is moored at the landing and is being loaded; the tide dial shows the time to the turn.
shots.question: Is it clear what the boat wants and how full it is?

shots.shows: The ford: people wade at low water (or wait on the bank at high water).
shots.question: Does the tide read as something you can see and use?

shots.shows: The far bank: the pasture with sheep, and the weaver on the near bank.
shots.question: Do wool and cloth fit the town?

shots.shows: The ferry in mid-river with riders, and queues on both banks.
shots.question: Does the ferry read as a bottleneck you would want to improve?

shots.shows: The drawbridge lifted for a boat, walkers waiting, the toll paid.
shots.question: Is the drawbridge with its toll worth being the last gift?

shots.shows: The shop in the second age, with the river's own group.
shots.question: Is the shop still readable with this many lines?

shots.shows: The town on both banks when the borough seal is granted.
shots.question: Does the town on the river look like a step up from the hamlet?

shots.shows: The page that closes the second age.
shots.question: Is this an acceptable ending for now?

sections.title: Zooming out to the book, and pausing

shots.shows: The closest view: tilted, so cottages and people show their sides.
shots.question: Do you want the tilted view when zoomed in?

shots.shows: Zooming out, first step: the whole town.
shots.question: Is this a good normal view to play in?

shots.shows: Further out: the whole page, with the interface thinned to a strip.
shots.question: Is the change of the interface at this point right?

shots.shows: Fully out: the open book on the table, the town's summary and achievements on the left page, the map on the right.
shots.question: Is this how the book should appear?

shots.shows: Pausing: the book half closed.
shots.question: Does pausing by closing the book feel right?

shots.shows: The closed cover as the pause menu: Resume, Settings, New town, Quit.
shots.question: Is the cover menu what you asked for?

shots.shows: New town asks once before replacing the town.
shots.question: Is this question worded and placed well?

sections.title: Settings, as pages of the book

shots.shows: Settings: Sound.
shots.question: Are these the volume controls you want?

shots.shows: Settings: Display.
shots.question: Are these the display options you want?

shots.shows: Settings: Keys, with a key being rebound and a clash to settle.
shots.question: Is rebinding clear?

shots.shows: Settings: Saving.
shots.question: Is the saving page complete enough?

shots.shows: The game at interface size 150 percent.
shots.question: Is the largest interface size usable?
